entities.name: Eccentric reaming limit
observations: Eccentric/asymmetric glenoid reaming is generally effective for correcting less than approximately 15 degrees of posterior glenoid retroversion; greater correction risks excessive bone removal and joint-line medialization.
A 13-degree retroversion is within the usual, borderline-acceptable range; 18–30 degrees generally exceeds the conventional limit.

entities.name: Reaming indication
observations: The appropriate deformity is mild posterior glenoid wear/erosion with limited retroversion in anatomic shoulder arthroplasty; severe posterior wear is not suitable for eccentric reaming alone.
Retroversion around 15–20 degrees may cause excessive medialization with eccentric reaming and favors augmentation, grafting, or another reconstruction strategy.

entities.name: Reverse arthroplasty distinction
observations: Reverse shoulder arthroplasty may use alternative techniques for substantial retroversion, but this does not make eccentric reaming appropriate at 25–30 degrees.
Severe deformity generally requires augmentation, grafting, custom reconstruction, or a different arthroplasty strategy.
